extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent applicants, patent agents, IP professionals, and IPOPHL examiners in the Philippines
extracted.subtask_description: Country-specific guidance on the Philippine patent system: what is patentable, filing and examination procedures (national & PCT), timelines, quality mechanisms, fees, accelerated routes, examiner training, and incentive/assistance programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable inventions (Rule 201, IRR)
rubrics_metrics.description: What kinds of subject-matter may be claimed as an invention under Rule 201, IRR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: a product (machine, device, article of manufacture, composition of matter, microorganism); a process (method of use, method of manufacturing, non-biological process, microbiological process); computer-related inventions (involving a computer, computer network or other programmable apparatus, with features realized wholly or partly by means of a computer program); and improvements of any of the foregoing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patentable inventions (Rule 202, IRR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories of subject-matter excluded from patentability under Rule 202, IRR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: discoveries and scientific theories; mathematical methods; abstract ideas; schemes, rules and methods for performing mental acts, playing games, or doing business; programs for computers; methods for treatment of the human or animal body by surgery/therapy and diagnostic methods practiced on the human & animal body; plant varieties or animal breeds or essentially biological processes for the production of plants and animals; aesthetic creations; and anything contrary to public order or morality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic requirements for filing an invention (Rule 400, IRR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal requirements for submitting a patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application may be filed in Filipino or English. Acceptable formats: handwritten, typewritten, computer-printed, or electronic filing via IPOPHL e-filing. Filed directly with Bureau of Patents (BOP duty officer) or by post. NOTE: All applications shall be addressed to the Director of Patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may apply for a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants for patent filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural persons and juridical persons (body of persons, corporation, partnership or other legal entity recognized by law) may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of resident agent/representative (Rule 421 & 421.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and rules for non-resident applicants to appoint a resident agent or representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A non-resident applicant must appoint and maintain a resident agent in the Philippines upon whom notices/process may be served. The application must contain the name and contact details of the patent agent/representative. A representative must be authorized to transact prosecution/maintenance and to address all communications from the Office. If multiple agents are appointed, the Office forwards actions to the last agent on record. A substitute/associate attorney may be appointed only upon written authorization of his principal; a third attorney appointed by the second will not be recognized. A power of attorney may be revoked upon proper notification; upon revocation the Office will communicate directly with the applicant or any newly appointed attorney/agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-file system (current regime, RA 8293): grant periods and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Core features of the Philippines' current first-to-file patent regime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Period of grant: Invention — 20 years from filing date or effective filing date; Utility Model — 7 years without extension; Industrial Design — 5 years, renewable for not more than two consecutive periods of five years each (renewal fee applies). Publication: 1st publication at 18 months after filing date; 2nd publication after grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old regime (first-to-invent, RA 165) — legacy differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison points for the old first-to-invent regime (historical/legacy cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the old regime: Invention — 17 years from grant; Utility Model — 5 years with possible renewals; Industrial Design — 5 years with renewals; publication occurred after grant (rather than 18-month first publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between invention and utility model
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational and substantive differences between patents (inventions) and utility models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventions: applications published with search report after 18 months; require formality and substantive examination; require inventive step; 20-year term; enforcement after grant; annual maintenance fees. Utility Models: published for 1 month prior to issuance of certificate; only formality examination (no substantive examination); do not require inventive step; 7-year term; enforcement determined by Registrability Report; no annual fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model registration process
rubrics_metrics.description: Process flow and timing for utility model registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formality requirements checked. If incomplete, action issued by examiner. If complete and compliant, recommendation for registration and publication (one month) followed by community review and third-party observation. If no adverse observation, issuance of certificate one month after publication. Two-month turnaround (UM in 2 months) is possible under regular route with complete compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design registration process
rubrics_metrics.description: Process flow and timing for industrial design registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formality requirements checked; examiner issues action if incomplete. If complete, recommendation for registration and one-month publication, community review and third-party observation. If none or resolved, issuance of certificate one month after publication. IPOPHL process can yield 'ID in 5 days' for certain cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and timeline for direct (national) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps and key time milestones for filing and prosecution of a national/direct patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stages: Filing -> Formality Examination & Search -> Substantive Examination -> Publication -> Grant/Refusal/Appeal. Early Search Report/Written Opinion available within 6 months. First publication at 18 months; applicants given 6 months from first publication to pay RSE if not paid earlier, otherwise application is withdrawn. Community review and third-party observations possible; appeals follow internal directorates up to courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for PCT applications (national phase entry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps when a PCT application enters the Philippine national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National phase entry involves checking for basic requirements, substantive examination, publication, and either grant or cancellation/refusal. The Office publishes listings of PCT applications that entered the national phase. Appeals and refusal procedures apply similarly to national route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination: refusal, amendment, and appeals flow
rubrics_metrics.description: How substantive examination handles refusals and the appellant path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner issues reasons for refusal, applicant is notified and may submit opinion and/or amendment. Decision to grant leads to 2nd publication and patent certificate. Final refusal by examiner can be appealed to Director of Patents, then to Director General, then Court of Appeal, and finally to the Supreme Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination — Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and benefits for requesting accelerated examination under PPH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH must be requested before substantive examination has begun. Benefits include faster prosecution of patent applications and acquisition of higher quality patent rights. IPOPHL provides details and forms on its website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination — ASEAN Patent Examination Cooperation (ASPEC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Features and benefits of ASPEC participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASPEC benefits include obtaining patents faster, reducing duplication of work, operation in English, and being free of charge to participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality mechanisms — in-process checks, ISO QMS, PQRS
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems IPOPHL uses to ensure quality and consistency of patent examination work products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-Process checks verify drafts for compliance with statutes, IRR and examination guidelines. IPOPHL has ISO 9001:2015 certification covering patents, UMs, IDs and trademarks to institutionalize systematic management and internal quality audits. Patent Quality Review System (PQRS) via the Quality Management Division (QMD) reviews examiners' work products (formality, search, substantive reports), updates the Patent Quality Manual, and recommends training.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-process review workflow (IPRS levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: The internal IPRS stages in the substantive report drafting and approval process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work products pass through IPRS I, II, III where substantive drafts are prepared, then IPRS IV drafts substantive examination report, and IPRS V does final check and approval before issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISO Certification 9001:2015 application
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope and role of ISO 9001:2015 certification in IPOPHL patent processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISO 9001:2015 covers processes of patents, utility models, industrial designs, and trademarks registration. It institutionalizes structures, mechanisms and standards for systematic business-process management and provides for internal quality audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulation and publication of specialized examination guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of field-specific examination guidance to ensure consistent examination approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPOPHL formulates and issues specialized guidelines such as 'Examination Guidelines for Computer- & ICT-Related Applications (2017)', 'Examination Guidelines for Applications in the Field of Biotechnology (2017)', 'Manual of Patent Examination Practice', and sector-specific guidance for pharmaceutical applications involving known substances and revised IRR implementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA/IPEA designation and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: IPOPHL's role as an International Searching Authority (ISA) and International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPOPHL is the 23rd ISA/IPEA in the world and 2nd in ASEAN; appointment was endorsed by JPO and AUPO. Designation indicates over 70 years of combined experience among examiners, capability in PCT receiving office functions, and patent examination practice comparable to international PCT standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Search Report (ESR) and Written Opinion (WO) service
rubrics_metrics.description: Features and operational details of IPOPHL's ESR & WO service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESR is a search report citing prior references to patentability; WO interprets findings. Features: expedited service with no request needed and no additional cost; SR and WO issued within 6 months (instead of 18 months); SR is published on the 18th month; the WO assists applicants to assess chances of securing a patent; applicants have 6 more months to decide whether to file an international application (PCT) which must be filed within 12 months from filing date. ESR & WO cover Filipino and foreign applications first filed with IPOPHL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competency-based training program for patent examiners (IPEST)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for examiner competency, induction and continuous training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuous training program for new recruits with 3 phases: Phase 1 (orientation, 4 months) covering QMS, IP basics, fundamental search & examination concepts; Phase 2 (6 months) follow-on seminars, mentoring, special topics; Phase 3 (4 months) assignment to examining divisions to apply knowledge in practice. Program includes advanced trainings, workshops, plant visits, partnerships with USPTO/EPO/JPO/WIPO, regional mentoring with IP Australia, and scholarships for advanced studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fees, payment policies, and discounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee structure and payment rules relevant to filing and prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: Filing Fee (inclusive of 5 claims) — Small Entity Php 2,000; Big Entity Php 4,320. Excess claims fee per claim Php 180 (small) / Php 360 (big). First and Second Publication fees (Php 920/960 depending on category). Issuance fees listed; 'FILE NOW and PAY LATER' option (pay within one month from filing). Plus 1% Legal Research Fund. Student/Youth filer discount: 75% off fees for filers 21 years and below. Annual fee schedules include on-time payment, late payment, 50% surcharge for publication fee late payment, and 1% Legal Research Fund components.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Filing Assistance Program — fee waivers and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: IPOPHL assistance measures to lower PCT-related costs for eligible applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistance may waive IPOPHL Search Fee (US$400 small / US$1,000 big) and Preliminary Examination Fee (US$200 small / US$500 big) and provide information/technical consultation. Eligible: individual Filipino inventor/applicant; Higher Education Institutions in the ITSO network; foreign inventors/applicants from States included in the WIPO List of Eligible Nationals or Residents for 90% reduction where IPOPHL is Office of First Filing for designated period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent/Utility Model/Industrial Designs Women Incentive Package ('Juana Invent/UM/ID')
rubrics_metrics.description: Special incentive to support women inventors and eligible small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver of filing fees in favor of 1,000 qualified applicants for: filing fees for Invention/UM/ID applications; filing fees for excess claims/additional embodiments for ID; first publication fee; and priority fee, if any. All other fees are to be paid by the applicant. Eligibility: Philippine nationals only or Philippine micro-, small-, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Search Report implementation performance (operational benchmark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational benchmarks and observed issuance rates for ESR & WO during pilot and rollout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot implementation began Nov 2016; full implementation starting 2018. Reported issuance: 146 of 182 applications (Jul–Dec 2017) and 191 of 239 applications (Jan–Jun 2018) (~80% in some periods). Shows practical benchmark for IPOPHL capacity to deliver ESR & WO within 6 months despite resource constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community review and third-party observation mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Public/community participation mechanisms post-publication that can affect grantability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After publication (1 month for UM/ID; 18-month for patents), there is a community review period during which third parties may submit observations. Existence of third-party observations can trigger further Office action and affect issuance; absence of observations allows issuance of certificate.
